item.title: Indonesian police arrest 72 people suspected of starting forest fires
item.summary: # Indonesian police arrest 72 people suspected of starting forest fires - Click here to listen to this article - Share via - Indonesian police have arrested 72 people suspected of deliberately setting forest and peatland fires to clear land cheaply, as investigators probe whether plantation companies financed the fires. - Fueled by El Niño and a prolonged dry season, more than 5,000 hot spots on Borneo and Sumatra have ignited widespread fires. - A ‘choking haze’ now blankets parts of Indonesia and neighboring Malaysia, reducing visibility, driving air quality to unhealthful levels and forcing officials to close nearly 600 schools, disrupting about 200,000 students. JAKARTA, Indonesia — Indonesian police on Sunday arrested 72 people suspected of starting some of the recent forest and peatland fires as huge blazes in central and western parts of the country triggered a harmful cloud known as a “choking haze.” Indonesia has been battling fires driven by an intensifying El Niño pattern and a prolonged dry season, generating dense smoke that crossed into Malaysia, according to Indonesia’s National Disaster Management Agency, or BNPB.
